title: Provide long-acting male contraception with demonstrated reversibility

concept.text: Prevent pregnancy for years after one procedure, with reliable restoration of fertility when contraception is no longer wanted. ADAM has completed an initial human study, but sperm suppression alone does not demonstrate reversible contraception. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval supported by at least two years of contraceptive effectiveness, fewer than 2 pregnancies per 100 couple-years, and a prospective reversal cohort showing sperm recovery in at least 90% within 12 months, with subsequent pregnancies documented. Test set by: A national regulator would decide approval; WHO's 2026 TPP explicitly addresses blockade of sperm transport. The duration, pregnancy-rate and recovery thresholds are proposed editorial criteria. Sources given: [WHO male contraceptive target product profiles](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240124950) ; [ADAM development status](https://www.contraline.com/trials) ; [ADAM registered human study](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05134428).

page.title: Reversible vas-occlusive male contraception
page.definition: A material placed in both vasa deferentia, the ducts carrying sperm, prevents pregnancy for years after one procedure. Fertility returns after the material is removed, dissolved or degraded.

goal.need: An estimated 164 million women want to delay or avoid pregnancy and use no contraception. About 30% of couples rely on a male method. Condoms and withdrawal require action each time a couple has sex. Vasectomy is intended to be permanent. A man who may want children later could take responsibility for contraception for years, including when his partner’s methods are unsuitable. Couples who also need protection against sexually transmitted infections would still have reason to use condoms.

completion.title: FDA authorizes multiyear vas-occlusive contraception with a fertility-restoration claim.
completion.criterion: FDA authorizes US marketing of a vas-occlusive device whose labeling covers pregnancy prevention for a specified multiyear duration after one placement and restoration of fertility after reversal or degradation. The FDA marketing decision and authorized labeling establish which claims are covered.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, device safety and effectiveness standard in 21 CFR 860.7 and applicable marketing authorization pathway.
completion.threshold_quote: reasonable assurance that the device is safe and effective for its conditions of use.
completion.basis: FDA evaluates evidence for the device’s intended conditions of use. Premarket approval and De Novo classification are possible routes, depending on the device. The multiyear duration and fertility-restoration claim specify the capability that the authorization must cover.

milestones.title: A safety board reviews the first five ADAM cohort 1 recipients 30 days after implantation.
milestones.criterion: The Data Safety Monitoring Board reviews safety data for the first five participants in cohort 1 at 30 days after ADAM implantation.
milestones.set_by: Contraline, ADAM protocol ADM-012, cohort 1, registered as NCT05134428.
milestones.threshold_quote: The first 5 subjects will be reviewed for safety by a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) at 30 days post-implantation.

milestones.title: A study reports rates of absolute and virtual azoospermia over the intended 1–3 years.
milestones.criterion: Use serial semen analyses to report separately the percentage of participants with no sperm in the ejaculate and the percentage with virtual azoospermia, defined as at most 100,000 non-motile sperm per mL. Assess persistence over the intended duration of 1–3 years.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 25.

milestones.title: A vas-occlusive method completes ≥200-couple efficacy testing and controlled human reversal testing.
milestones.criterion: EAA/ASA recommend ≥200 couples completing one year of pregnancy follow-up, longer for multiyear use; safety cohorts of ≥300 men for a 1-year device and 100 followed for 3 years; and randomized multicentre evidence of reversibility. A 2023 RISUG analysis included 303 of 315 treated men and recorded 8 pregnancies through 7 years; authors attributed 4 to method/drug failure. A 1992 polyurethane-plug cohort reported pregnancies in partners of all 130 selected men within 0.5–4 years after reversal, following 0.5–5 years of occlusion. Neither report is a randomized reversal trial.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, section 8.2, Values and recommendations 23–24.
milestones.threshold_quote: reversibility in randomized-controlled, multicenter clinical trials in men.

milestones.title: An intravasal material blocks sperm passage in an animal model and permits it again after reversal.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate obstruction of sperm passage with the material in place, then detect sperm passage in the same animal after reversal. This measures reopening of the duct. Recovery of the ability to sire offspring is a separate outcome.
milestones.set_by: Preclinical vas-occlusion studies by Uniyal and Laumas and by Waller and colleagues, using return of sperm passage as the endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: restore sperm concentrations in ejaculates after a reversal procedure.

milestones.title: The Plan A reversal cohort measures return to baseline semen levels in 10 men.
milestones.criterion: In the 10-man reversal cohort, document absence of sperm after occlusion, perform the reversal procedure and report how many men return to baseline semen levels. Follow participants for up to three months after reversal or until baseline levels return. The endpoint measures semen recovery.
milestones.set_by: Next Life Sciences, Plan A Occlusion and Reversal System Feasibility Study, protocol CIP102, NCT07361120.
milestones.threshold_quote: Total number of subjects (N=10) that return to baseline semen levels after reversal

milestones.title: At least 200 couples complete one year of pregnancy follow-up, with longer follow-up for multiyear use.
milestones.criterion: Measure the pregnancy rate while couples rely on the vas-occlusive method for contraception. At least 200 couples complete one year of follow-up. Extend follow-up beyond one year for a method intended to work for several years.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 23 and section 8.2 supporting evidence.

milestones.title: Safety follow-up covers ≥300 men for a one-year device and 100 men followed for three years.
milestones.criterion: Record adverse events in at least 300 men for a one-year device and follow 100 men for three years. Record procedure-related and device-related events at insertion and reversal, including recovery time, swelling and discomfort.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 24.
milestones.threshold_quote: 300 men for a 1-year device and 100 men followed for 3 years.

milestones.title: Randomized controlled multicentre trials demonstrate reversibility of vas occlusion in men.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate reversibility in men in randomized controlled multicentre trials. Identify the recovery outcome measured so that return of sperm to semen and subsequent pregnancy can be judged separately.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, section 8.2, Values.
milestones.threshold_quote: reversibility in randomized-controlled, multicenter clinical trials in men.

results.finding: RISUG efficacy study: 8 pregnancies were reported among partners of 303 analyzed men.
results.detail: The authors attributed four pregnancies to method or drug failure. The study reports no controlled human reversal testing, and the text does not specify how many couples completed follow-up at each time point.
results.quote:
A total of 8 pregnancies were reported but 4 of these pregnancies had
  social cause as their husbands were showing persistent azoospermia
  and remaining were due to method failure (0.3%, n=1) and drug
  failure (0.98%, n=3).

results.finding: Intravas devices: 972 men received an implant; follow-up exceeded 92% in each device group.
results.detail: The trial included follow-up at 12 months after surgery, with condoms used for the first 3 months. It reports no controlled human reversal testing. The devices filter sperm without completely obstructing the vas.
results.quote: There were 487 (IVD-A), 485 (IVD-B) and 487 (NSV) male volunteers who received either IVD-A, IVD-B or NSV operation, respectively. The follow-up rates in the three groups were all greater than 92% ( Table 1 ), which fulfilled the needs of the project design.

results.finding: ADAM hydrogel with 10–20 nm pores was reported to block sperm passage. Sample size unstated.
results.detail: The text does not specify how sperm passage was assessed in the permeability evaluation.
results.quote: The vas-occlusive hydrogel demonstrates selective permeability with a pore size of 10 to 20 nm, effectively preventing sperm passage while allowing diffusion of small molecules.

results.finding: The ADAM implant and its degradation products showed no adverse findings across four reported toxicity endpoints. Sample size unstated.
results.quote: The implant and its degradation products were found to be noncytotoxic, nonirritating, nonsensitizing, and nongenotoxic.

results.finding: In the 25-man first-in-human ADAM trial, 2 men reached azoospermia at 24 months.
results.detail: The article identifies 25 men in the 90-day safety analysis. The number assessed at 24 months is unspecified.
results.quote: According to the press release from Contraline, 2 participants have become the first to reach azoospermia at 24 months.

results.finding: The first-in-human ADAM trial recorded 76 adverse events in 25 men during 90 days of follow-up.
results.detail: The article draws on a conference abstract and reports events of any attribution.
results.quote: During the 90-day follow-up, 76 adverse events were recorded, with 84.2% classified as mild, 14.5% as moderate, and 1.3% as severe, all anticipated.

results.finding: Two ADAM trial participants reached absolute azoospermia at 24 months.
results.quote: In The ADAM Study, two participants are the first to reach azoospermia at 24 months

results.finding: The ADAM study reported zero treatment-related serious adverse events in its 24-month update. Sample size was unstated.
results.quote: No treatment-related serious adverse events (SAEs) have been reported.

results.finding: Among 303 men analyzed after RISUG injection, 97.3% had azoospermia at one year.
results.detail: The reported oligozoospermia category has no stated sperm concentration cutoff.
results.quote: reached to the highest level of 97.3% after 1-year post-injection.

results.finding: In the RISUG trial of 303 couples analyzed, 0.98% had pregnancies attributed to drug failure.
results.detail: The paper’s 99.02% pregnancy-prevention estimate counts only pregnancies attributed to drug failure.

results.finding: In the RISUG safety cohort of 303 men, 55.4% had mild to moderate scrotal swelling at day three.
results.detail: The 303 men are the overall analysis cohort. The paper gives a maximum follow-up of seven years without stating the three-year completion count.
results.quote:
Similarly, in 55.4% subjects mild to moderate scrotal swelling was
  observed on 3rd day post RISUG injection

results.finding: Animal IVD experiments found that most sperm were blocked and that rabbit vasal patency was higher after IVD removal than after anastomosis. Sample sizes and rates were unreported.
results.detail: The journal article describes these animal observations as unpublished. The reported patency comparison does not give a paired sperm-passage measurement.
results.quote: The patency rate of the vas lumen achieved in reversal operations was higher in IVD removal than in vas anastomosis (unpublished).

results.finding: In 972 IVD recipients, serial semen testing through 12 months found lower azoospermia rates than after no-scalpel vasectomy.
results.detail: The supplied text names the sperm concentration table but omits its cells, so the absolute azoospermia percentages cannot be extracted.
results.quote: The azoospermic rates at 3 rd –6 th  and 12 th  month post-operation both in groups IVD-A and IVD-B were lower than those in the NSV group in this study because of the different contraceptive mechanisms.

results.finding: Among 487 IVD-A recipients and their partners, the reported pregnancy rate was 0.65% within 12 months after surgery.
results.detail: The abstract and discussion give the quoted IVD-A rate. The Results section also states that no additional pregnancies occurred during the exposure period, creating an internal discrepancy.
results.quote: There was a 0.65% pregnancy rate in the IVD-A group within 12 months postoperatively.

results.finding: Among 485 IVD-B recipients, the reported cumulative complication rate was 0.9% at 12 months after insertion.
results.detail: The complication assessment included short-term events such as bleeding and infection and longer-term events such as granuloma and congestive epididymitis.
results.quote: The cumulative rates of complications at the 12 th  postoperative month were zero, 0.9% and 1.7% in the three groups, respectively.

results.finding: Sperm returned to the ejaculate in all 7 Vasalgel-treated rabbits after reversal.
results.detail: Two rabbits had only one vas deferens flushed. The return of sperm confirms reopening of at least one duct in each rabbit.
results.quote: Spermatozoa were observed in the ejaculates of all subjects at an average of 23.7 ± 9.3 days after the reversal procedure.

results.finding: In male rabbits (n=20 across four reversal groups), sperm reappeared in ejaculates 60–75 days after reversal of RISUG-induced azoospermia.
results.detail: Semen was sampled every 15 days. The paper reports results by group.
results.quote: Spermatozoa reappeared at 60–75 days of reversal and normozoospermia was noticed between 135 days and 150 days in the reversal groups.

results.finding: Candidate EVOH vas-occlusive polymers underwent MEM elution cytotoxicity testing. Sample size and numerical outcome are unspecified in the excerpt.
In the 23-recipient ADAM trial, the Data Safety Monitoring Board recommended continuing without modification. The number of recipients covered by its review is unspecified.
results.detail: The 23 recipients are the trial-wide implantation count across two cohorts.
results.quote:
Contraline’s Data Safety Monitoring Board,
chaired by Dr. Larry Lipshultz, Professor of Urology at Baylor College of Medicine, concluded
that the safety of ADAM is excellent and the study should continue in its current form without modification.

results.finding: In a Phase III RISUG study of 28 men, 25% had absolute azoospermia 3 weeks after injection.
results.detail: Follow-up extended to 5 years, but the paper provides no visit-specific denominators or azoospermia rates for years 1–3. The reported mean sperm counts cannot establish how many men met the virtual azoospermia threshold.
results.quote:
Our results demonstrate that just after 3 weeks of RISUG
®
injection majority of subjects,
that is
more than 75% of the subjects show severe oligospermia and 25% of subjects showed azoospermia.
